text:
emma: Heads-up — we pushed canary v2 at 10% but telemetry shows a subset of users getting 100% canary for multiple minutes. Not all users, looks correlated with header X-Rdwd-Region.
ryan: Huh. Was the canary wired to header routing? The rollout was supposed to be hash-based sticky sessions at 10%.
alisha: We have a header rule for experiments that routes by X-Rdwd-Region for EU traffic, but it's supposed to be lower priority than the split guard. checking config...
deploy-bot: deploy event: service=inference-api, env=prod, tag=canary-v2, user=alisha, ts=1802001099 :rocket:
maria: Logs show requests with header X-Rdwd-Region: eu-west-1 are short-circuiting to canary because header-match rule evaluated before split guard. Example trace: decision=header_match -> route=canary-v2.
ryan: Can you paste the relevant routing block?
alisha: here is the route fragment from rollout.json:
```
"routes": [
  { "priority": 10, "match": { "header": { "X-Rdwd-Region": "eu-west-1" } }, "route": "canary-v2" },
  { "priority": 20, "match": { "split": { "hash": "user_id", "weights": { "stable": 90, "canary-v2": 10 }, "sticky_cookie": "inference_session" } }, "route": "weighted" }
]
```
alisha: the bug is that lower numeric priority means higher precedence in the runtime (priority 1 runs first). someone inverted the ordering when converting console -> spec. so header (10) runs before split (20).
maria: that explains it. Console shows the split with 10% but does NOT show match rules ordering in the rollout summary. very confusing for on-call.
sre-oncall: impact: intermittent traffic skew for certain regions. Customer reports about latency differences may be from canary. Suggest hotfix: change header rule to priority 30 or make split guard "evaluate_first": true.
ryan: Quick hotfix: flip priorities in prod config and restart router? How invasive is that?
alisha: small -> pushing change to routing store now. also adding a guard: "match.meta: require split_evaluation" so header won't override unless explicitly marked.
emma: Also a UX follow-up: console should surface evaluation order and an "effective routing" preview for a sample user (headers + cookie + ip). Right now the UI only shows static blocks which hides precedence.
maria: Agree. Also we should log the "routing_decision" per-request to telemetry with which rule matched and evaluation order, at least for 48h. That would have made this visible immediately.
sre-oncall: adding runbook note: when investigating skew, check routing_decision in traces, then config priorities.
ryan: filing two tickets: 1) fix priority inversion for header rules (hotfix) 2) console enhancement + per-request decision trace. assigning to @alisha and @maria.
alisha: assigned, will cherry-pick hotfix in 5m.
deploy-bot: deploy event: service=inference-api-router, env=prod, change=priority-fix, user=alisha, ts=1802001400 :white_check_mark:
emma: thanks. after hotfix i'll re-run synthetic canary checks and watch split stability. :eyes:
maria: postmortem note: UI->spec roundtrips should validate semantics like "priority ordering preserved". small mismatches lead to surprising routing.
ryan: good catch by @maria noticing header correlation. closing for now but keep watchers on telemetry for 30m. :thumbsup:
